title: A Year of Helping Others
task: In your English class you have been talking about young people and their communities. Write an essay using all the notes and give reasons for your point of view. Essay question: “Young people in the Lake Kingdom should spend a year helping their community before university or work. Do you agree?” Notes: 1. skills and experience 2. money 3. ……… (your own idea). Write 140–190 words.

points.label: Note 3: your own idea
keys: re:\b(another|a further|a third|finally|lastly|last but not least|moreover|furthermore|what is more|in addition|additionally)\b

model:
Many people believe that a year of community work is the perfect bridge between school and adult life. However, is it really a good idea for everyone?

Firstly, a year spent helping others can teach valuable skills. Young people who work in hospitals, schools or lake clean-up teams learn to communicate, solve problems and take responsibility, and these experiences are often more useful than anything learnt from a textbook.

On the other hand, money is a serious concern. If volunteers are not paid, students from poorer families may not be able to afford a year without a salary. As a result, the scheme could become something only rich families can enjoy.

Another point to consider is that some young people already know exactly what they want to study. For them, a compulsory year might feel like a delay rather than an opportunity.

In my opinion, a community year is an excellent idea, but it should be optional and every volunteer should receive a small wage. That way, everyone could benefit.

p: I look forward to hearing from you.

title: Screens or Storybooks?
task: In your English class you have been talking about reading. Write an essay using all the notes and give reasons for your point of view. Essay question: “Children today spend too much time on screens and not enough time reading books. Do you agree?” Notes: 1. imagination 2. learning 3. ……… (your own idea). Write 140–190 words.

points.label: Note 3: your own idea
keys: re:\b(another|a further|a third|finally|lastly|last but not least|moreover|furthermore|what is more|in addition|additionally)\b

model:
These days it is hard to find a child who does not own a tablet. But are screens really taking the place of books?

To begin with, reading develops imagination in a way that screens rarely do. When children read a fairy tale, they have to picture the castle and the dragon themselves, whereas a cartoon shows them everything.

However, it would be unfair to say that screens are bad for learning. Educational apps and videos can explain difficult ideas clearly, and many children have improved their vocabulary by watching programmes in English.

What is more, the problem is not the screen itself but how it is used. A child who reads e-books on a tablet is still reading, while a child who plays the same game for hours is not learning much at all.

In my view, children do spend too much time on screens, but the answer is balance rather than banning them. Parents should make time for books every day, especially at bedtime, so that reading becomes a pleasure, not a duty.

p: I look forward to hearing from you.

title: Review: The Glimmerfin Water Show
task: You see this announcement on the Lake Times website: “Reviews wanted! Have you seen a show, film or performance recently? Tell us what it was about, what you liked and didn't like, and whether you would recommend it.” Write your review in 140–190 words.
model:
The Glimmerfin Water Show: a splash of magic!

If you're looking for an unforgettable evening, head to Crystal Lake. The Glimmerfin Water Show tells the story of a young fish who is chosen to protect the lake from a mysterious storm, and it is performed by dancers, acrobats and hundreds of lights on the water.

What impressed me most was the final battle. Fountains shot thirty metres into the air while the music grew louder and louder, and the whole audience gasped. The costumes were stunning too, especially Glimmerfin's silver scales, which seemed to change colour as she moved.

However, the show was not perfect. The first half was a little too long, and some of the jokes were clearly written for very young children. I also wish the seats had been more comfortable, as we had to sit on hard wooden benches for two hours.

Overall, I would highly recommend it to families and anyone who loves spectacular effects. Just remember to bring a cushion!

title: Making Friends in a New Town
task: You see this notice in an English-language magazine: “Moving to a new town? How can people make new friends after moving? What worked for you? Is it easier to make friends online or in person?” Write an article answering these questions in 140–190 words.
model:
New Town, New Friends?

Have you ever stood in a new street and realised that you didn't know a single person? It's a lonely feeling, but it doesn't have to last long.

The secret is to go where people with the same interests meet. Joining a club or a sports team gives you something to talk about straight away, and volunteering is a brilliant way to meet kind, friendly people. Even saying hello to your neighbours can open doors.

When I moved to Crystal Lake two years ago, I found it hard at first. Then I signed up for a rowing class, and after a few weeks I was invited to a barbecue. Most of my closest friends today were sitting in that boat with me!

So, is it easier online or in person? Social media can help you find events and stay in touch, but in my experience real friendships grow face to face. A chat on an app is nice, but nothing beats laughing together over a cup of hot chocolate.

p: I look forward to hearing from you.

title: Report: Improving the Lake Youth Club
task: The manager of the Crystal Lake Youth Club wants to improve it. Write a report for the manager saying what is good about the club now, what problems members mention and what you recommend. Write 140–190 words.
model:
Introduction
The aim of this report is to describe the strengths of the Crystal Lake Youth Club, to outline the main problems mentioned by members and to recommend some improvements.

Current strengths
The club is currently very popular, with over eighty regular members. Most people enjoy the friendly atmosphere, and the boat trips on Saturdays are described as the highlight of the week.

Problems
However, several members complain that there is not enough to do on weekday evenings. In addition, the games room is outdated: the computers are slow and the table-tennis equipment is broken. A lack of quiet space also means that it is difficult to do homework at the club.

Recommendations
I would recommend replacing the old computers and repairing the games equipment as soon as possible. It would also be a good idea to turn the small storeroom into a study area. Finally, I suggest organising a weekly cooking or music workshop, which would attract more members during the week.

Dear Mr Reed,

I am writing to apply for the position of Summer Lake Guide, which I saw advertised on your website. I have loved Crystal Lake since I was a child, and I would be delighted to share its secrets with visitors.

As for experience, I have been a member of the lake rowing club for three years, and last summer I volunteered at the nature centre, where I led short walks for primary school groups. This taught me how to keep a group safe and interested at the same time.

I believe I would be suitable for the role because I am patient, reliable and confident when speaking to strangers. I also speak English, Spanish and a little French, which could be useful with international tourists.

I am available from the end of June until the beginning of September, including weekends.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Elena Ruiz

title: Should Every Student Learn to Cook?
task: In your English class you have been talking about the skills young people need. Write an essay using all the notes and give reasons for your point of view. Essay question: “Every student should learn to cook at school. Do you agree?” Notes: 1. health 2. independence 3. ……… (your own idea). Write 140–190 words.

points.label: Note 3: your own idea
keys: re:\b(another|a further|a third|finally|lastly|last but not least|moreover|furthermore|what is more|in addition|additionally)\b

model:
Cooking lessons have disappeared from many school timetables. Should every student learn to cook before leaving school?

Firstly, cooking is closely linked to health. Students who can prepare simple meals are less likely to live on crisps and fizzy drinks, and they discover which foods give them energy for sport and study. If everyone knew how to make a quick vegetable soup, far fewer teenagers would skip lunch.

Secondly, cooking builds independence. Having learnt to follow a recipe, young people can look after themselves when their parents are busy, and they feel more confident about helping at home.

Another point to consider is that cooking is great fun. A class that has baked bread together has not only practised weighing and measuring, but also learnt to work as a team.

On the other hand, it is often argued that timetables are already too full. However, a single lesson every two weeks would be enough to make a real difference.

In my opinion, cooking should be taught in every school, because it is a skill that lasts a lifetime.

p: I look forward to hearing from you.

title: Review: Starfall Builders
task: You see this announcement on a website for young gamers: “Reviews wanted! Tell us about a game you have played recently. What is it about, what did you like and dislike, and who would you recommend it to?” Write your review in 140–190 words.

points.label: Who you would recommend it to

model:
Starfall Builders: a game that is out of this world

If you've ever dreamed of building your own space station, Starfall Builders is the game for you. Players crash-land on a tiny planet and must gather crystals, grow food and build a base before the next meteor shower arrives.

What impressed me most was the teamwork mode. Up to four friends can play together, and each person has a special job, such as engineer or plant scientist, which means that nobody is left out. The music is relaxing, and the planets are stunning, with glowing purple forests and floating islands.

However, the game is not perfect. The instructions at the start are confusing, and I wish there had been a proper tutorial. I also found that the later levels became repetitive, because you build the same kind of tower again and again.

Overall, I would highly recommend it to anyone aged nine and over who enjoys creative games. It is ideal for rainy weekends with friends, although you should remember to take a break every hour!

title: The Best Club at My School
task: You see this notice in your school's English magazine: “Which club at your school would you recommend to a new student? What do members do there, and why is it worth joining?” Write an article answering these questions in 140–190 words.
model:
Why Not Join the Garden Club?

Have you ever eaten a strawberry you grew yourself? If not, the Garden Club at Hillside School could be just the place for you.

Every Wednesday after lunch, about twenty members meet in the corner of the playground, where we look after six vegetable beds and a small pond. In spring we plant seeds, and by the summer holidays we are picking tomatoes, beans and sunflowers taller than our teacher! Last year some of our pumpkins were sold at the school fair, and the money was used to buy three bird boxes.

So why is it worth joining? Firstly, you do not need any experience, because the older members are happy to show you what to do. Being outside in the fresh air is also a brilliant way to relax after a busy morning of lessons.

Most importantly, you will make friends with people from every year group. If you are looking for a club that is fun, calm and useful, why not come along next week?

title: Tips for Space Camp
task: Read the email from your friend Jake and the notes you have made. Write your reply to Jake using all the notes. Write 140–190 words.

email.text: Our class is going on a three-day trip to a science and space camp next month, and I'm a bit nervous because I've never been away from home. You went last year! What was it like, what should I pack, and have you got any tips?

model:
Hi Jake,

Thanks for your email. I'm so excited for you, because the space camp was honestly the best trip I've ever been on!

On the first day we built rockets out of plastic bottles and launched them on the field. Mine flew higher than the teacher's, which I'm still very proud of. In the evening we looked at the stars through a huge telescope, and I saw the rings of Saturn for the first time.

As for packing, make sure you bring warm clothes, because the nights get really cold. You should also take a torch, a water bottle and a good book for the coach.

My biggest tip is not to worry about being homesick. I was nervous too, but once the activities started I was having too much fun to think about it. If I were you, I would also keep a short diary, so you can remember everything afterwards.

Write soon and tell me how it goes!

Best wishes,
Maya
